svg.aria-label: Diagram: what-if, preflight validation and deployment history in Azure, showing the three validation levels Provider ProviderNoRbac and Template, the seven change types what-if reports, the five kinds of expression it cannot evaluate, the limits at which it stops expanding nested templates and marks the remainder Ignore, the difference between deployment what-if as an operation and stack what-if as a stored result resource, and the 800-deployment history limit
svg.title: What-if predicts, preflight checks and history records — three different questions, and what-if is honest about what it cannot evaluate
svg.text: A prediction, a precondition check and a record. Three different questions.
What-if says what would change, preflight says whether it could run at all, and history says what actually happened.
One switch decides how much checking happens before the prediction
Provider
the default — syntax, resources, dependencies, and whether you may deploy them
ProviderNoRbac
the same, but checks read permission only — for previewing without deploy rights
Template
static only — skips preflight and permission checks, so it misses what would fail
Preflight is the part that asks the resource providers. Turning it off makes the preview faster and less true.
Seven change types
Create
not there yet; will be made
Delete
complete mode only
Ignore
exists, not in the file — or a limit was hit
NoChange
redeployed, nothing differs
NoEffect
read-only property the service ignores
Modify
redeployed, properties differ
Deploy
redeployed, and it does not know whether
anything changes — ResourceIdOnly format
Five things it cannot evaluate
Nondeterministic functions such as newGuid() and
utcNow()
Any reference to a secure parameter value
References to resources not deployed in the same
template, or to properties not defined in it
Any resource function, such as listKeys()
And reference() is never resolved, so a property set
from it is reported as changing every single time.
Those are the false positives the output calls noise.
Where the prediction quietly stops
What-if expands nested templates until it reaches 500 nested templates, 800 resource groups in a cross-resource-group deployment,
or 5 minutes of expansion. When one of those is reached, everything remaining is marked Ignore — which reads like “nothing will
happen here” and means “this was not analysed”. templateLink is not expanded at all, so template specs never appear.
Deployment what-if is an operation
You run it, Azure returns the predicted changes, and
nothing is stored afterward.
Add it to a deployment as a confirmation prompt with
--confirm-with-what-if
or PowerShell’s
-Confirm
so the preview and the approval are one step.
Stack what-if is a resource
It creates a what-if result resource you name, of type
Microsoft.Resources/deploymentStacksWhatIfResults
so it can be retrieved, shared by resource ID, and
deleted. It reports Detach as well as Delete.
Keep retention at PT3H or less — longer results are
never deleted for you, and each one is a resource.
And afterwards: the history, which is also a budget
The deployment history for a resource group is limited to 800 deployments, and as you near the limit deployments are automatically
deleted from the history. Every deployment carries a correlation ID, which is what Azure support asks for to find the failed operations.
The error message lives on the deployment operation, not the deployment: filter operations by the Failed state to reach the real cause.
Sources: Bicep what-if, Preview deployment stack changes with what-if, and Deployment history, on Microsoft Learn.
